content.thinking: I'm going to fix the issues I found, starting with the root cause: the code removes a check for zero that it needs. Next I'll rewrite the range expressions using "over" and "during" in the chain step.

action_items.item: Turn monthly-spend-feature off for io-shop until the proposed fix is merged and deployed.
Find out how monthly-spend-feature was switched on without appearing in the flag provider's history or the production change events.
Make every flag change on io-shop go through the flag provider so it is recorded in the history Argus reads, and close any path that switches flags outside it.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page.
Require tests that run each flag-gated code path with its flag on, including shoppers with past purchases but none this month, before the flag can be enabled in production.
Make flag rollouts on io-shop stage through traffic slices, and pause or revert automatically when the error rate rises.

causal_chain.step: The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. That error first appears in the logs at the onset and nowhere before it.

ruled_out.what: A revision rolled out to only some replicas, sending some requests down a different path: at {T10.1} all {T10.2} replicas ran one revision.

causal_chain.step: The monthly-spend-feature flag began evaluating on. Every evaluation logged during {G7e5d.4} was off. At {G971b.6} some evaluations were on, and the logs show it on during {Gce95.4}. The switch appears in no change record Argus read: the production change events returned {T9.2} changes, and the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus. What switched the flag is not in the record. No deploy or other change was recorded, so none could be ruled out by the service being measured healthy with it in place.
Turning the flag on sent account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month down a code path that divides by their number of purchases this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A setting that adds a monthly spending summary to account pages came on, and nothing Argus read records who or what turned it on; the summary's code likely fails when it works out an average for shoppers who have bought before but bought nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: The switch of monthly-spend-feature to on was not recorded in the production change events or the flag provider's history, so Argus had no recorded change it could undo and refused to act on C1.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Had the switch been recorded, Argus could have turned the flag back off during the response. That would have stopped the failing account pages instead of leaving the flag on for a person to deal with.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Once Argus left undoing the flag to a person, a paged on-call engineer could have turned the flag off and shortened the incident.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that exercised the flag-gated monthly summary for a shopper who has bought before but not this month before the flag was turned on. Code-Fix reports that the existing tests call this shopper the ordinary case and their own helper builds one.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would have raised ZeroDivisionError before the flag reached production, and the flag would not have been turned on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from on for part of traffic to on for all of it, and no guard was seen that held or reverted it while the account page error rate rose.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A rollout held at the first slice, or reverted on the rising error rate, would have limited the failures to a small share of shoppers or ended them soon after they began.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at the minute the logs show the flag first evaluating on.
The Investigator Agent formed candidate C1, which named the monthly-spend-feature flag and the ZeroDivisionError the logs show.
Argus did not act on a change that was missing from the record of what changed, and left undoing it to a person.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #540 for a person to review.

went_wrong: No mitigation was applied during the response: the flag was still on and account pages were still failing when the incident was escalated to a person.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` (as long as `use_typical_spend` is false). That function divides the account's total for this month by the number of its purchases marked `in_current_month`. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has none, so the division is by zero and their account page request raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.
input.still_at_risk: While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers who had bought before but not this month, and the flag could be switched again without showing up in any change record Argus reads.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for some shoppers
